corrected_value.authors: Borreggine, K. L., & Kaschak, M. P.
corrected_value.title: The action–sentence compatibility effect: It's all in the timing.

decisions.quote:
As a first step in assessing the replicability of motor
compatibility effects, we conducted a pre-registered, multi-lab
replication of the ACE. We used an adapted version of the
original ACE paradigm (Glenberg & Kaschak, 2002) that was
used in Borreggine and Kaschak (2006). The choice of this
particular version of the ACE paradigm was somewhat arbitrary. We had no strong a priori reasons to expect that one
paradigm or the other would produce a stronger or more reliable ACE. Ultimately, we chose the Borreggine and Kaschak
(2006) paradigm over the original Glenberg and Kaschak
(2002) paradigm in part because we sensed that this paradigm
would be slightly easier to execute across a large group of
labs.
decisions.reason: Under the codebook rule on replication chains, when a finding has already been re-tested or adapted by others, the target is the study closest to this paper in the chain that it actually re-tests rather than the chain's original source. The authors explicitly state that they chose to replicate the adapted version of the ACE paradigm and critical sentences from Borreggine and Kaschak (2006) over the original Glenberg and Kaschak (2002) paradigm, making Borreggine and Kaschak (2006) the tested original study.

decisions.quote:
We undertook a multi-lab, pre-registered replication of the
ACE to determine whether the effect could be produced reliably using a standard paradigm in the field. The results of the
replication effort are clear: This version of the ACE was not
statistically significant in any of the individual studies, and the
meta-analytic effect size was close to zero (see Fig. 6).
decisions.reason: Both shipped and blind codings agree that the replication outcome is 'failed'. Across all 18 participating laboratories (12 native English-speaking and 6 non-native English-speaking), no lab observed a statistically significant ACE on lift-off times or movement times, the meta-analytic estimate was close to zero and within the pre-registered negligible range, and the authors explicitly conclude that their study failed to replicate this version of the ACE.

decisions.reason: Both shipped and blind codings agree that the record type is 'replication'. The study collected new experimental data from 1,492 participants (1,278 after exclusions) across 18 laboratories to re-test the published action-sentence compatibility effect.
